text:
Openjutsu

An open-source, Genjutsu-style character and object swap for video. Drop a video and a character photo, press Generate , and the main person in the video is replaced by your character. Or change their hair or clothes, remove something, or put them somewhere else. The camera, cuts, motion and soundtrack stay. Everything runs on open weights on your own GPU: MiniMax H3 for the video, SAM 3.1 to track people, and Qwen3-VL 8B to describe the pictures and shots.

The app is a small Next.js front end over a ComfyUI workflow. It uses @comfyorg/sdk , following Comfy's comfy-reshoot reference app.

 

 Advanced: several people, pick who becomes who Object swap: paint where it goes 
 --- --- 
 
 From picture: a new look and place from one picture Post-processing: fix faces 
 

 From picture → Relight: new light in the same pass 

 

 First visit: visual describer

The welcome page lets you choose the vision-language model that describes pictures and video frames and writes prompts. Qwen3-VL 8B INT8 remains the default; Qwen3-VL 4B FP8 and Gemma 4 E2B INT8 are smaller alternatives. Install a compatible single-file model including its vision weights in ComfyUI/models/text encoders , then press Refresh models . Other installed models can be selected if they support image/video input and text generation through ComfyUI's CLIPLoader and Generate Text nodes. Text-only models and files requiring a different loader are unsuitable.

Choose according to available VRAM and leave room for image/video context and working memory; file size is not a VRAM requirement, and H3 generation has separate memory needs. Your selection is saved in this browser and used for swaps, prompt descriptions and Find people . Reopen Welcome & models to change it, or use Visual describer under Model components. Alternative describers may change prompt quality and person matching. Set up later opens the editor; generation still checks the required files. The separate H3 text encoder remains unchanged.

 Modes

- Simple motion transfer : available. One character replaces the main person (the one who fills the most of the frame). Runs workflows/simple.api.json , exported from H3 One-Click Single Swap (DMAD 6 step).json .
- Advanced motion transfer : available. 1–4 characters, each with an optional role; every tracked person is matched to a role per shot, and people without a character stay untouched. Runs workflows/advanced.api.json , exported from H3 One-Click Advanced Swap (DMAD 6 step).json ; One pass per person (two characters) runs workflows/advanced maxq.api.json .
- Object swap : available. Change what SAM tracks (hair, a jacket, a car) into what you describe or show in a picture; Remove it; or change the Background around it ( person stays). Only that area is regenerated. Runs workflows/object.api.json , exported from H3 One-Click Object Swap (DMAD 6 step).json .
- From picture (under Object swap): FLUX prepares the character in the raw video frame's pose and body cut while keeping the character picture's background. Review or regenerate the image, then choose Use this image to set the video length, video and motion-reference resolutions, models, LoRAs, steps and seed. SolarRenderer defaults to four steps with a selectable rank-384 or rank-64 four-step/control pair and supports up to 15 seconds, like the native H3 renderer. SolarRenderer clips longer than six seconds can take considerably longer to render, especially at higher resolutions; see the workflow requirements for the extended-silence node fix. Both LoRA file pickers support models/loras and its subfolders. Use this image also has the visual describer watch the part and write what happens (actions, held objects, expressions), then rewrite it for the prepared picture; check and edit that video description before rendering. Render video reuses the saved preview with normal-map motion guidance, the video description and the source soundtrack, in one clip without a context loop. H3 rounds the requested length down to its valid frame grid. Relight (off by default) changes the light in the same FLUX pass: pick one of seventeen looks, each shown with an example picture, or describe your own light. FLUX then sees only your picture, and the Qwen 3.5 9B prompt upsampler reads the pose from the video frame. Magenta club and Teal lasers mostly recolour the background. Relight the video's own person skips the character picture: FLUX relights the video frame itself, keeping its person, pose and setting. See the workflow requirements.
- Post-processing : available, for a finished video. Fix faces : H3 draws faces poorly when the person is small in the frame, so this redraws the face of the person in a photo at close-up size and pastes it back. Runs workflows/face.api.json , written by workflows/build/openjutsu face build.py . Fix colours softens H3's harsh look without an H3 run: Image Detail Contrast takes some fine detail contrast out, then Orion4D's DCTL Tone Mapper grades every frame. Runs workflows/color.api.json .

 Requirements

- An NVIDIA GPU. Tested on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB with 64 GB of system RAM; the H3 int8 models stream from RAM.
- ComfyUI 0.41.2 or newer. Core provides MiniMax H3, SAM 3.1 and TextGenerate.
- Node.js 22.6 or newer, and Python for comfy-api-proxy .

 Custom nodes

Install these into ComfyUI/custom nodes (ComfyUI Manager finds the first three by name):

 Pack Used for 
 --- --- 
 SolarRenderer From picture: SolarRenderer LoRA loading, conditioning and four-step sampling 
 ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-Context-Loop 0.7.3+ clip loop, checkpoints, final assembly 
 ComfyUI-Fantastic-MiniMaxH3-PromptBuilder masked video-edit latent 
 ComfyUI-KJNodes Grow Mask With Blur; From picture: VRAM cleanup 
 comfyui controlnet aux From picture: Metric3D normal maps 
 ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite video loading 
 comfyui-h3-oneclick-swap swap and object plans, people and role masks, grey mannequins, track labelling, cut finder, shot list, face-fix chunks 
 ComfyUI-H3-FaceRefi

install.title: Deploy on the Comfy Developer Platform
install.html:
Not tested yet. The app code does not change, only .env.local:

  1. Package the prepared ComfyUI install (with the custom nodes and models above) as a Build, and deploy it:

    pip install comfy-cli
comfy setup --where cloud
cd /path/to/ComfyUI
comfy build init --name openjutsu --models-dir ./models --custom-nodes-dir ./custom_nodes
comfy build status
comfy build push --release --target linux/nvidia
comfy deploy refs compute

  2. Create a deployment from the released Build on the Developer Platform. The workflow has only been run on a 16 GB card with 64 GB of system RAM, so choose at least that.

  3. Set COMFY_BASE_URL to the deployment URL and COMFY_API_KEY to a key from the workspace that owns it. The key stays on the server; never put it in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable.

  4. Before hosting or tunneling the app, set a strong OPENJUTSU_PASSWORD and use HTTPS. Without a password, Openjutsu refuses to start on any address but loopback. It also refuses a password shorter than 12 characters. After 5 wrong passwords a client must wait before each try, from 1 second doubling to 5 minutes; clients are told apart by their X-Forwarded-For address, which only a proxy or tunnel that sets it makes reliable, so 20 failures spread across clients make everyone wait too. Open the page and sign in as openjutsu with that password; the same browser login protects uploads, job controls, progress and downloads. This is a single-owner app: everyone given the password shares access to its jobs. The start-up check cannot see a tunnel or reverse proxy on the same machine, so never point one at a password-free server.

  5. Host the Next.js app anywhere that runs Node. npm start listens on 127.0.0.1 only; to serve on a network address, build and start Next with the password set (Next uses PORT if the host sets it, otherwise 3000):

    npm run build
OPENJUTSU_PASSWORD='<strong password>' npx next start --hostname 0.0.0.0

    Streaming progress needs a host that keeps long responses open. Preserve the public Host and scheme when reverse proxying so same-origin API checks work.

Notes:

  • Resuming relies on clip checkpoints in ComfyUI's output/ folder, which a fresh serverless worker does not have.
  • A job runs for many minutes; check the deployment's request time limit.
  • Stop or delete the deployment when you finish, to end GPU charges.
